messages:
kevin_sales: Quick thread for MedSys POC network - they need an outbound-only setup from their AWS account in us-east-2. Looping @raj_neteng and @maria_se.
amanda_cust: Hi - we're MedSys. VPC CIDR 10.30.0.0/16. Security requires no route propagation into our VPC. PrivateLink preferred; can you confirm firewall allowlist steps and any expected IPs? Also need estimate for 14-day POC: ~30GB/day.
maria_se: PrivateLink is our recommended approach. Short checklist: provide AWS account ID, VPC ID, two private subnet IDs (one per AZ), firewall change window. We'll provide the ENI private IPs once the endpoint is created.
raj_neteng: Implementation notes: we create an NLB + service in our Redwood account. Customer creates an Interface Endpoint that attaches ENIs in their selected subnets. Egress: TCP 443 to the ENI private IPs. DNS (UDP 53) if you use internal resolver. No inbound rules required on your side.
amanda_cust: Do you support pre-sharing IPs? Our firewall team prefers IPs ahead of time.
raj_neteng: ENI IPs are stable after endpoint creation. If they need IPs in advance, they can temporarily allow TCP 443 to the subnet CIDRs you plan to use and tighten after we supply the ENI IPs.
sec-bot: Security pointer: we can add mTLS if MedSys requires mutual auth for the POC. Also ask for SOC contact if they want us to complete their questionnaire.
maria_se: Pricing: AWS charges per-interface-endpoint-hour + per-GB processed. For 14 days at ~30GB/day, expect modest AWS costs; we'll include a line item in the POC quote. If cost becomes blocker we can propose short-lived peering as alternative (requires route updates).
kevin_sales: Next steps: 1) Amanda confirm 2 private subnet IDs + firewall window. 2) Raj to provision NLB/service and share NLB name. 3) Maria to prepare one-page checklist and small cost note. Raj ETA ~24h.
amanda_cust: Thanks all - I'll get subnet IDs and SOC contact later today.
kevin_sales: Great, ping here when ready and we'll spin up the endpoint.
